profile.summary: HyPLM-Flash is a masked protein language model of 652 million parameters. It reads one amino acid sequence, up to 8,190 residues in a single window, and returns a 1280-dimensional vector per residue, a pooled vector, or masked language model logits that can be turned into a zero-shot variant score. It keeps the 33 token alphabet and the output head of ESM-2, so it can stand in for ESM-2 in an existing pipeline, and it ships with its own GPU inference engine that uses INT8 matrix multiplication and padding-free batching.

summary_quotes.text:
HyPLM-Flash is a 650-million-parameter masked language
model trained on 726 billion tokens

The model has 32 layers of width 1,280 with 20 attention heads and a
SwiGLU width of 3,584, for a total of 652 million parameters, and reads proteins of up to 8,190 residues
in a single window.
It keeps the vocabulary and output head of ESM-2, so it can replace ESM-2 in existing pipelines

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: It is a bidirectional transformer encoder trained by masked language modelling: 15 per cent of residues are selected, 80 per cent of those replaced by a mask token, 10 per cent by a random amino acid and 10 per cent left as they are. Each of the 32 blocks puts RMSNorm before self-attention with per-head query and key normalisation and rotary positions, then before a SwiGLU feed-forward layer, each inside a residual connection. The output head is RoBERTa style: a dense layer, GELU, LayerNorm, then a linear map to 33 logits. The block weights were trained with the Muon optimiser and everything else with AdamW.

sections.title: Training data and decontamination
sections.body: The corpus combines UniRef90 with the UniRef50 representatives it does not contain, MGnify90, the active entries of UniParc and the non-redundant isolate proteomes of JGI IMG. Sequences of 30 to 8,192 residues are kept, exact duplicates are removed across sources, and the sequences of the benchmarks used during development are removed by exact match, including all ProteinGym wild types and variants. That leaves 2.6 billion sequences, or 659 billion residues, sampled in proportion to length, so metagenomic and archival sequences supply about 80 per cent of the tokens. Pretraining covers 713 billion tokens on crops of up to 1,022 residues; a second stage of 13 billion tokens extends the crops to 8,190 residues and adds auxiliary structure objectives on 1.6 million chains, with those chains first filtered against the test proteins by MMseqs2. The auxiliary heads are used only during training.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One checkpoint is released, version 1.0.0 of the hyplm package, with the report dated 12 October 2026. The 2.6 GB of FP32 weights come as two shards from the repository's GitHub Releases under the tag hyplm-flash-weights; the download script merges them and checks the sha256 against ce7dcd4fc473dc334d869718a9a31149573893795db03c45efeb396e8b180ab1. A result must also name the precision, because the engine runs INT8 by default and BF16 on request. The developers state that zero-shot, structure, function and likelihood metrics agree within 0.01 between the two, while representations of variants of the same protein differ by about 1 per cent, so they advise BF16 when training regressors on such data.

sections.title: What the developers report
sections.body: The report states a ProteinGym zero-shot Spearman correlation of 0.409, which it calls statistically tied with ESM-2 650M, ESM C 600M and E1-600M, the best long-range contact precision of all models it evaluated, and about 130,000 residues per second embedded on one NVIDIA H20, 1.9 to 2.7 times faster than other encoders of the 600M class. The comparison is a matched evaluation of 28 public checkpoints from 13 model families on 32 tasks. These are the developers' own figures and have not been reproduced by Rewire.

run_guide.summary: Download the weights, install the package and get embeddings and a masked-marginal mutation score.
prerequisites: A CUDA GPU, Hopper such as an H20 or H100 recommended, and Python 3.10 or later.
curl for the weight download; a GitHub token only if the API rate limit is hit.
About 2.6 GB of disc space for the FP32 weights.
torch 2.4 or later, safetensors, triton and flash-attn, which the package install pulls in. Code and weights are MIT.

steps.title: Get embeddings
steps.shell:
python3 - <<'PY'
from hyplm import HyPLMEncoder

encoder = HyPLMEncoder.from_pretrained("weights")       # INT8 by default
sequences = ["MKTAYIAKQRQISFVKSHFSRQ", "ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY"]

residue = encoder.encode(sequences)                     # list of [L, 1280]
pooled = encoder.encode(sequences, pooling="mean")      # list of [1280]
print(residue[0].shape, pooled[0].shape)
PY

steps.title: Score one mutation
steps.shell:
python3 - <<'PY'
from hyplm import HyPLMEncoder

encoder = HyPLMEncoder.from_pretrained("weights")
sequence = "MKTAYIAKQRQISFVKSHFSRQ"
logits = encoder.logits(sequence, masks=[2])[0]         # [L, 33]; residue 3 is replaced by <mask> first
log_probs = logits[2].log_softmax(-1)
tokens = encoder.tokenizer.tokens                       # vocabulary order
score = log_probs[tokens.index("V")] - log_probs[tokens.index("T")]   # masked-marginal score of T3V
print(score)
PY

notes: Points for a reviewer. The parameter count is 652 million in the report's Section 2.1 and Table 1, while the README and the abstract round it to 650 million; the structured row uses 652000000. The released date is the date printed on the report's title page, 2026-10-12, not a stated release date for the weights. The weights_url in the structured row is the first of two shards, since the sources give no single file URL; weights/download.sh merges the shards and verifies the sha256 ce7dcd4fc473dc334d869718a9a31149573893795db03c45efeb396e8b180ab1. The record's existing sources are pinned to commit 0dcc533c and this page uses the same commit, although the repository's default branch has since moved to b24e7f5543f08069fe190e98c5c05b62ca28a074. The report's accuracy and speed claims are the developers' own, from their own matched evaluation, and the decontamination claim (every ProteinGym wild type and variant removed by exact match) also rests on their word. Every quote from the report comes from a pdftotext text layer, so line breaks inside quotes follow the PDF layout.
